content: Hi all! A few days ago we shared the Lean Workspace project in #Project announcements > Lean Workspace — a shared workspace where human teams and AI agents collaborate to write proofs together. I'm opening this topic as a home for questions and discussion.
Hi Shannon, could you explain how the agent is it designed, and how is it different from other coding agents (e.g. codex, opencode) and self-improving agent (e.g. hermes)?

Qingyuan Zhao said:

Hi Shannon, could you explain how the agent is it designed, and how is it different from other coding agents (e.g. codex, opencode) and self-improving agent (e.g. hermes)?

Thank you Qingyuan!

  1. We do not redesign the agents themselves -- you literally use claude code / codex in the lean workspace -- but we build this collaboration layer for such agents to (1) make the agent work structured, (2) enable easy team agent collaboration, and (3) better coordinate long-form tasks
  2. As for "self-improving agent", I think the biggest differentiating factor is that we include all the harness-code, memory and rubrics in the repo itself. Therefore, during the course of the working on a repo, it can (1) customize the harness for the specific project that you are working on, (2) accumulate your project specific memory and rubrics and (3) using the rubrics to guide the agents implementation (see this example).
